stimulus.source_note: Bartolome de las Casas, A Brief Account of the Destruction of the Indies (written 1542, published 1552; this English translation, 1689). Text verbatim from Project Gutenberg EBook #20321. Archaic spelling kept.
stimulus.text: Finally, in one word, their Ambition and Avarice, than which the heart of Man never entertained greater, and the vast Wealth of those Regions; the Humility and Patience of the Inhabitants (which made their approach to these Lands more facil and easie) did much promote the business: Whom they so despicably contemned, that they treated them (I speak of things which I was an Eye Witness of, without the least fallacy) not as Beasts, which I cordially wished they would, but as the most abject dung and filth of the Earth.

stem: Las Casas describes Native peoples as humble and patient, and says he saw the cruelty himself. Which statement best evaluates how useful this account is as evidence of Native American societies before contact with Europeans?

options.misconception: Assumes moral judgment makes a description accurate.
options.text: Because Las Casas judged the conquest by universal moral standards, his account gives a reliable, modern-style description of Native societies before Europeans arrived.

Las Casas wrote to move the king to reform colonial policy, so the account is best evidence of the Spanish debate over Native treatment; for describing Native life itself, it must be checked against other sources.

options.misconception: Makes violence the only cause and ignores disease.
options.text: The account proves that Spanish violence was the single cause of the collapse of Native populations in the Caribbean, since Las Casas saw firsthand why so many Native people died.

options.misconception: Generalizes one region to the whole Americas.
options.text: Las Casas described the Native people he knew in the Caribbean as peaceful and gentle, so his account can safely be generalized to show that Native societies across the entire Americas were nonviolent and untouched by conflict.

instruction: Answer from the stimulus and stem only. Pick one option. Do not open the question file.
